A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PPTArena and PPTPilot. Their complete main texts and appendices, including tables, diagrams, examples, and prompt listings, support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original agent evaluations and ablations in Tables 3–4, plus cross-judge and T2US experiments in Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark experiments and adds human evaluations, judge-consistency measurements, and a page-wise scoring control in Sections 5.2–5.3 and Appendix E.2.

M1.justification: The semantic planning, routing between programmatic and XML editing, validation, and reflection procedures are retained. SSIM screening and the detailed two-stage editing paths already appeared in v1's appendix. Updated backbone versions are experimental configuration changes; no new algorithmic component or procedure is established.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate PPTArena's 100 decks and 2,125 slides across the same editing taxonomy, plus T2US and PPTC-R. Revised edit totals and sourcing-pool sizes do not establish additional task or domain coverage. The human and batching studies assess existing editing tasks.

E2.justification: v3 adds Kimi-K2.6 to the matched subset comparison and reports Gemini CLI and ChatGPT alongside the subset baselines in Table 4. The other principal comparators remain. The earlier Poster2Agent label corresponds to Paper2Poster, which remains reported in v3's text and Appendix Table A.

E3.justification: Reported configurations change from GPT-5/Gemini 2.5 Pro to GPT-5.2/Gemini 3.1 Pro, and the T2US backbone changes from Gemini 2.5 Flash to 3.0 Flash. The hard-subset selection description shifts from poor model performance to structural difficulty plus breadth. v3 also reports 1,340 edits rather than 800+, introduces a blind 25-expert evaluation on a stratified 10% subset, and adds a 105-slide-pair page-wise control. These are documented setting changes and new protocols, without establishing which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds substantial validation of the evaluation pipeline: human–judge alignment, repeated-call consistency, and batched versus page-wise visual scoring. It also reports the router's 66% programmatic versus 34% XML usage. The executor ablations, alternative-judge comparison, and illustrated failure cases already existed in v1 and are largely retained.

E5.justification: v1 provides no corresponding repeated-judge uncertainty analysis. v3 Table 8 first reports five judge runs per example, majority agreement of 78%/95% for IF/VQ, and standard deviations reported as 15.4%/9%. It also introduces Pearson, Spearman, and Kendall human–judge correlations. This adds statistical validation and variability reporting, rather than establishing an increase over a previously specified run count.

E6.justification: PPTPilot's full-benchmark IF/VQ changes from 2.36/2.69 to 2.57/2.69, and its subset scores from 1.71/1.54 to 1.87/1.91 (v1 Table 3; v3 Tables 4–5). v3 adds Kimi scores, human ratings, latency measurements, and judge-validation outcomes; reported average operations change from 5.1 to 13.4. The ablation and T2US scores remain unchanged. Revised models and settings prevent interpreting the changed scores as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Neither version presents new theoretical propositions or proofs. The existing scoring rubrics and diff-computation logic are retained; the added correlation and consistency measurements are empirical statistics, not new mathematical results.

C1.justification: The benchmark, hybrid editing agent, claimed performance advantage, and remaining long-horizon difficulty remain the central contributions. v3 revises the advertised scale from 800+ to 1,300+ edits and explicitly strengthens the benchmark contribution to include validation against human experts. The introduction also adds a statistical-power claim based on comparisons with other agent benchmarks.

C2.justification: v3 explains ChatGPT Agent's relative advantage on Structure tasks through native GUI handling, contrasting this with PPTPilot's tendency to over-edit master XML. It also adds a plateau-based rationale for the three-pass refinement cap. The detailed failure examples and limitations concerning ambiguous instructions, cross-application workflows, and specialized domains are retained.

D1.justification: New Appendix I and Table D document baseline interfaces, backbones, context limits, retry budgets, timeouts, latencies, and an approximately $700 evaluation cost. Appendix J changes the release statement from planned to released and specifies screenshots, structural diffs, judge prompts, and raw outputs. These substantially expand reproducibility information, although availability itself cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v3 adds an explicit comparison with the concurrent, independent PPTArena benchmark, contrasting its GUI tasks over 12 source files with this work's scope. It also adds SWE-bench Multimodal scale positioning and a Kimi reference. Much of the extensive bibliography revision supplies author, title, and publication metadata for already cited works rather than changing research positioning.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is substantially reorganized: detailed ablations move from main Section 5.2 to Appendix E.3, difficulty analysis moves into the main benchmark section, and separate sections present judge reliability and human comparisons. The abstract, conclusion, and dataset explanation are rewritten or expanded, and the title, author list, and bibliographic text are revised.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. v1 Figures 2–3 are merged into v3 Figure 2, the pipeline diagrams are redrawn, and the main results are separated into subset and full-benchmark tables. New latency, human-validation, and configuration tables accompany extensive resizing and restyling of appendix figures and code listings.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens a central weakness of v1: automated evaluation lacked measured human alignment and judge repeatability. The expert study, repeated-judge analysis, and batching control directly support the benchmark's credibility, while matched comparisons and baseline budgets improve interpretability and reproducibility. Reporting problems temper these gains: revised counts and configurations are not fully reconciled, and Figure G retains older PPTPilot scores despite Tables 4–5. These limit precise performance interpretation but do not outweigh the substantial new validation.
